name: Sparse autoencoder feature steering
description: Training and applying sparse autoencoders to decompose polysemantic neurons into interpretable monosemantic features, then using those features to steer model behaviour at inference time via residual stream interventions.

name: Circuit analysis and attention head identification
description: Identifying the minimal sets of attention heads and MLP layers that implement specific algorithmic functions — induction, copying, factual recall, name-binding — using activation patching, path patching, and output weight analysis.

name: Superposition and polysemanticity in neural representations
description: Investigating how transformer models represent more features than available dimensions via near-orthogonal superposition, characterising the geometry of feature co-representation, and the conditions that drive polysemanticity versus monosemanticity.

name: Activation patching and causal tracing
description: Using activation patching (causal tracing) to localise where specific information — factual associations, syntactic roles — is stored and computed in transformer architectures, across model families and scales.

name: Surface code architecture and threshold analysis
description: Designing surface code architectures optimised for realistic hardware noise models, and deriving and computing error thresholds that determine whether a surface code can suppress logical error rates below physical error rates.

name: Fault-tolerant gate synthesis
description: Synthesising universal logical gate sets — in particular T gates and CNOT gates — with full fault-tolerance guarantees, using magic state distillation, code switching, or transversal gate constructions.

name: Magic state distillation protocols
description: Developing and optimising distillation protocols that purify noisy magic states (T states, CCZ states) to high fidelity for use in fault-tolerant T gates, with focus on reducing qubit-time overhead.

name: Neural and algorithmic decoding for quantum error correction
description: Developing fast, accurate decoders — both classical matching algorithms and learned neural decoders — that process syndrome measurement outcomes and infer correction operations for surface codes and related stabiliser codes in real time.

name: Single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing and dimensionality reduction
description: Developing and evaluating methods for quality control, normalisation, and dimensionality reduction of scRNA-seq count matrices, with particular attention to preserving rare cell type structure and enabling downstream clustering and annotation.

name: Gene regulatory network inference from single-cell data
description: Inferring directed gene regulatory networks — transcription factor to target gene relationships — from scRNA-seq expression profiles, using statistical, graphical model, and deep learning approaches calibrated against CRISPR perturbation ground truth.

name: Cell trajectory inference and pseudotime analysis
description: Computationally recovering the temporal ordering of cells along differentiation trajectories from static snapshot scRNA-seq data, including branching trajectory reconstruction and pseudotime assignment.

name: Chromatin accessibility and multimodal single-cell integration
description: Analysing scATAC-seq data to map open chromatin regions, calling differential accessibility peaks, and jointly embedding scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq modalities to connect regulatory accessibility with gene expression.
